trails.title: Camera training
trails.subtitle: the store to the camera head
trails.say: From the features-only store to the camera head: the recipe names it, every row becomes the 393 values it reads, the booster grows its trees, the candidate holds it, and promote moves it into live only behind the battery.

entries.anchor: case "scratch": c = c.scratch(trees: trees ?? 500, eta: eta ?? 0.04)

Plans the recipe and prints the plan, then trains it into a candidate unless --plan asked only for the plan.

entries.anchor: for member in recipe.ordered { metrics[member.name] = try member.train(in: run) }
entries.note: Copies the parent bundle into a candidate, then asks each member of the recipe to train, in dependency order, and verifies the candidate. The engine knows no member by name.

entries.anchor: let dataset = try CameraDataset.assemble(run.store, settings: settings)

entries.note: Stacks each row's plain DINOv2 embedding and nine capture values in id order, with the trainer's row weights, and marks the held-out new-generator rows and the evaluation rows.

trails.title: Specialist training
trails.subtitle: the store to the heads and the combiner
trails.say: From the store's DINOv2 rows to the linear heads and the combiner that pools them: each head is a logistic regression split by source and admitted only if calm real photos stay real, and the combiner is a bounded fit around the camera head whose rescue is swept against the protect-real probes.

Holds out a quarter of the sources, drawn by CPython's own shuffle, so a retrained head is tested on the same sources the shipped one was.

entries.note: Fits the anchor's weight and the three evidence weights with reals counted three times, then chooses the rescue weight by the sweep. On 2026-10-21 no candidate kept the top probe under 0.42, so the rescue took the fallback, 1.0.

entries.note: Tries rescue weights 0, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0 and 1.3 and keeps the first under which every protect-real probe reads real and none above 0.42; with none, the fallback.

trails.title: Shared Signals
trails.subtitle: everything the stack reads, computed once
trails.say: The second stage: one object holds what every member of the stack reads, each computed once on first use: the screenshot gate, the capture reading, the two DINOv2 readings and the patch tokens. The Stack stage reads them next.

steps.title: One object, built once an image

entries.note: Holds the image and the config; the gate is computed now, every other signal lazily and once, so no member measures a signal twice.
A cheap measure of flat UI: few colours, hard edges and text-like rows, read on a capped copy of the image. The screenshot member reports it.
The native-resolution capture measurement, cached for the camera member and the capture member.
One measurement in two forms: the nine values the camera head reads, and the signature, present at a peak of 30 or more on a short side of at least 512.
The plain reading, short edge 256 and a centre crop of 224, which the camera head reads.
DINOv2-small's CLS embedding of the plain input.
The force-resized reading, 360 by 640, which every linear head reads.
The same backbone after a forced resize, so a phone screenshot's size cannot leak into the heads' embedding.
DINOv2's 256 patch tokens of the plain input, read once for the semantic tiles member.
The same forward pass as the plain reading, kept at the token level: a 16 by 16 grid of 384 values each.

trails.title: Stack
trails.subtitle: every member speaks, each with its own score
trails.say: The third stage: the pipeline declares its members and runs each on the shared signals: the screenshot gate and head, the camera head, the capture signature, the art, blur, human and preview heads, and the semantic tiles. No member reads another's output; the Revisions stage does.

entries.note: The shipped detector as one declaration: the stack's members in order, then the revisions in order. A new member is one file and one line here.
Computes the signals once, collects every member's output, then runs the revisions in order and returns one result that lists both.
Asks every member in turn; a member with nothing to say for this bundle or profile leaves no entry.

steps.title: A member and what it reports

entries.anchor: func score(_ s: DetectionSignals) throws -> MemberOutput?
entries.note: What a member is: a name and one function from the shared signals to its own output.
A member's take: its P(AI), its verdict and the fields only it reports, written into the result as they are.

entries.anchor: let p = head.predict(CameraRow(dino: dino, capture: capture).asVector)
entries.note: The camera head on the 393-column row, called at 0.5 with a band of 0.04, and p_neutral, the same head with the capture flags set.
The capture signature as measured: the peak, whether the image is large enough to read it, and whether it is present. It measures, so it has no P(AI).
The gate's three tells and the screenshot head's P(AI) on the force-resized embedding. It reports on every image; the combiner anchors on it when the gate fires.
One file for the art, blur, human and preview heads, each its own row of the stack; a head the bundle lacks leaves no entry.
A standardized logistic regression over the 384 values, the whole of a linear head.
The semtile head on each of DINOv2's 256 patch tokens: a 16 by 16 grid of P(AI) and the share of tokens above 0.5, its majority.

trails.title: Revisions
trails.subtitle: three revisions that read the stack
trails.say: The fourth stage: the combiner anchors on the camera member, or the screenshot member when the gate fired, silences the generated-side evidence under a present capture and otherwise pools it; the frame seam reruns the pipeline on a dark frame's interior; the preview tail flips a small image to real only when two reads agree. The Result stage writes what they leave.

steps.title: The combiner: the anchor and the pool

entries.note: Takes the anchor's P(AI) and operating point; a present capture leaves the anchor standing, otherwise the combiner pools it with the evidence members its file names.

entries.anchor: if a < anchor.gateCeiling { z -= rescue.w * max(0, -maxLogit) }
entries.note: Adds each evidence member's generated push to the capped anchor logit, and subtracts the consensus rescue only while the anchor sits under the gate ceiling. On 97,181 capture-absent store rows, taking the human push out moved 68 calls.
Caps each evidence member's logit at 2. The reference combiner also let an art-pair head lower the art logit; taking it out moved 29 of 97,181 store calls, 19 of them to the right label.

An evidence member's influence, recorded in the combiner's record: its generated push, or, while every member reads real under the gate, the shared rescue. Without the rescue a real wildlife photograph flipped to generated on 2026-10-19.

steps.title: A dark frame hiding the content

entries.note: When a real verdict hides a uniform dark border, runs the whole pipeline again on the interior and takes that evidence only when it is decisive. In the 2026-10-19 census it ran on 3 of 300 images and decided one, IMG_0500, a hard battery image.

entries.anchor: guard [imgTop, imgBottom, left, right].filter({ $0 }).count >= 2 else { return nil }
entries.note: Reads a 96×96 luma grid and calls a frame when at least two border bands are dark, uniform and darker than the interior.
A small image read generated with a clean semantic majority flips to real only when the preview member and the camera member's p_neutral both read it real. It fired once in the 2026-10-19 census.
Commits the flip only under the production profile; the diagnostic profile records that it fired and leaves the verdict.
The camera head asked again with the capture signature's validity flags set, so a small image's missing capture cannot read as generated.

Serializes the result as schema-v1 JSON with JSONSerialization and sorted keys, the bytes the goldens and the battery read.

trails.title: Watermark signing
trails.subtitle: an image to its signature, nothing added to it
trails.say: From an image to its watermark, with nothing added to its pixels: the native plane is cut into 32-pixel tiles, the warp residual gives each tile a fragility rate, each tile becomes four ordinal bits against its neighbours, sixteen tiles pack into a 64-bit word, and the words are named by their SHA-256.

steps.title: The command reads the image at its own size

entries.note: veilgarde watermark sign prints the signature as one line of vw1 text, or as JSON with --json, and names its grid, its bits and its id on stderr. Nothing is written into the image.
Signs an image with nothing added to its pixels: its tile codes at native resolution, read from the grid anchored at the top-left corner.

entries.anchor: let pixels = try ImageLoading.rgbPixels(cg, width: cg.width, height: cg.height)
entries.note: Reads the RGB plane once at its native size, with no cap and no padding. A crop must land on the same pixels in the same tiles as its source, and a resize would move every one.

steps.title: Every tile's fragility, by the warp residual

entries.anchor: let fr = WarpResidual.fragility(low: low, high: high)
entries.note: Measures every full tile's fragility rate from a given origin: each batch of tiles warped at both strengths, the residual read, the rate taken.
The forward and inverse tap tables for both strengths, built once per process: they are constants.
Builds the table pair for the weaker strength and the stronger one.
Moves a tile's four corners by the fixed displacements times the strength, and keeps the reference's inverse of the inverse for the way back, cast once from float64.
The 16 homographies as corner moves in [−1, 1], a literal table: every signature ever written was read through these warps.
The round trip through the 16 homographies and back, the error averaged over channels and trials, then a 9×9 Gaussian high-pass at σ 1.5.
A tile's fragility rate: how much more of it the stronger warp loses than the weaker, per unit of strength.

entries.anchor: if v > g[nr, nc] { bits[r * g.cols + c] |= 1 << k }
entries.note: Turns each tile's fragility into four ordinal bits against its east, south, south-east and north-east neighbours, masking every comparison that leaves the image. An ordinal bit survives any monotone change of the residual's gain.
entries.cite: test:tile codes: four ordinal bits against E, S, SE, NE, masked at the edges

entries.note: A signature holds its version, 32-pixel tiles, 4-tile sections, the tile grid's rows and columns, and the packed words.
Four by four tiles, 128 pixels, pack into one 64-bit word in row-major order, with a mask word beside it. No hash folds them, so a bit that differs is one bit of distance, not a different word.
The one line sign prints: vw1: and the binary in base64url.

entries.anchor: for w in codes { withUnsafeBytes(of: w.littleEndian) { d.append(contentsOf: $0) } }
entries.note: The binary: a magic, the version, the tile and section sizes, the grid's rows and columns, the section count, then every code word and every mask word, little-endian.
The id is the SHA-256 of exactly those bytes, so two signatures of the same pixels are the same id.

trails.title: Watermark matching
trails.subtitle: a crop or a re-encode to its place and score
trails.say: From an image and a signature to a match: the signature is read back and checked, the image's codes are read at sixteen grid phases, each phase slides over the signature at every whole-tile offset, the best agreement is the match, and the acceptance and the invariance run hold the signatures to their record.

steps.title: The image is read at sixteen grid phases

entries.note: The defaults: a phase every 8 pixels, a match at 0.75 over at least 256 compared bits, and offsets that run one tile past every edge.

entries.anchor: out.append((px, py, TileCodeGrid(plane.fragility(originX: px, originY: py))))
entries.note: A crop starts at an arbitrary pixel, so its tiles straddle the signature's. Its codes are read from 16 origins, every 8 pixels in each direction, which puts one within 4 pixels of the signed grid.

entries.note: The same measurement as signing, from a shifted origin: only the tiles that fit whole past it.

steps.title: Each phase slides over the signature

entries.anchor: guard let b = Matcher.best(crop: crop, stored: stored, margin: options.margin, minimumBits: options.minimumBits) else { continue }
entries.note: For each phase, asks the matcher for its best whole-tile offset, and keeps the best score over every phase, more compared bits breaking a tie.

entries.anchor: public var tileCodes: TileCodeGrid { Sectioning.unpack(codes: codes, masks: masks, rows: rows, cols: cols) }
entries.note: Unpacks the section words back into the tile grid, so the matcher compares tile against tile.
Slides the crop's codes over the signature's at every whole-tile offset and counts the disagreeing bits among those both sides measured; the offset with the best score wins.

steps.title: The best agreement is the match

entries.note: How far the score sits above chance, in coin-flip units for the bits compared. It does not replace the 0.75 floor: every crop that compared 256 bits scored at least 9.2 above chance, but strangers reached 11.9, since the matcher keeps the best of thousands of placements.

entries.anchor: public var pixelX: Int { offsetX * WarpConstants.tileSize - phaseX }
entries.note: Where the image's top-left corner sits on the signed image: the offset in tiles times 32, less the phase.
veilgarde watermark verify gives the same verdict as an exit code: 0 for a match, 1 for none.

steps.title: The acceptance and the invariance hold v1 to its record

entries.anchor: let report = try WatermarkAcceptance.run(sample.map { ($0.url, $0.label) }, settings: settings, note: note,
entries.note: veilgarde watermark accept samples final_mixed by a seed, half real and half generated, and writes each image's row as it is measured, so a long run that stops keeps what it measured.
Draws the same images from the same seed as the 2026-10-19 run did, each label shuffled by its own seeded generator.

entries.anchor: let cross = Watermark.match(codes: cropCodes, against: other, options: options)
entries.note: Signs every image, then measures each: a self-match, a crop of half its area at a random pixel offset, a JPEG at quality 0.75, the crop against the next image's signature, and on every fourth image the crop resized.
The share of ones at each bit position. On 198 images every position sat between 0.496 and 0.498, so no bit is close to a constant.

The kill criterion, fixed in code before the run: the crop must match with its offset in 60% of images, the median JPEG score must reach 0.75, and some threshold must reach 80% crop recall with at most 5% false matches. On 198 images v1 passed with 73.2%, 0.958, and 81.3% recall at 0.73 with no false match, on 2026-10-19 and again on 2026-10-21 after the residual moved.
Signs the battery's 105 images again and lists every way a signature departs from the recorded one. After the detection change and after the residual moved, all 105 were equal.
